Comments: On June 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Cowden 11H OG Well located on the Cowden 15 well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County following IR 4139773, where violations were issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on site. Big Dog Energy (BDE) is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 15 well pad, however, according to Department records, Diversified owns both the well pad and the gas wells on this well pad. During this inspection, the following was observed:An Act 9 sign was observed at the access road entrance, all information that is required to be posted on the Act 9 sign appears to be BDE's. Both on-site mailboxes which were attached to the Act 9 sign were observed to be empty at the time of this inspection. (Photos 1-3). Violations issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on-site is being continued at this time.A paved access road was observed to lead to the Cowden 15 gas well pad. No erosion and sedimentation issues were observed.The Cowden 15 gas well pad is located behind a chain-linked fence that was locked at the time of this inspection (Photo 4). The rest of this inspection was conducted from outside of the locked fence.3 gas wellheads with well tags fixed to them were observed on this gas well pad (Photo 5).3 production tanks within secondary containment were observed on this gas well pad. Other production equipment within secondary containment was observed on site. (Photo 7-8).A white storage tank was observed on site and appears to be connected for production. (Photos 9-10)Labeled barrels were observed to be within secondary containment. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on site is being continued at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 981838
Permit API: 015-23622
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Leroy Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/17/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "SGL12 L South" Marcellus well site.Chesapeake finished hydraulically fracturing the 3 Marcellus wells here in October 2022.Tony Savitski (Chesapeake) called the DEP on Monday January 16, 2023 (yesterday) to report an estimated 20 gallon spill of produced liquid from a vac truck to the pad surface. Chesapeake removed the visually impacted pad material and staged it on liner containment on the north corner of the pad. That material returned a >4.00 mS/cm electrical conductivity (EC) reading. I spoke with Andy Steffe and Ryan Carmody (both Creston Environmental) on site. They are screening the excavated area near the production tank for EC with a Hanna Groline Soil Test soil probe. I used the same model soil probe in the excavated area also. Both meters maxed out (>4.00 mS/cm), indicating residual production liquid impact from the spill yesterday morning. Background pad material gave 0.07-0.19 mS/cm readings. Creston is collecting solid samples from the excavated area, and from the waste material on the liner.Violations for the produced liquid spill are cited to the 015-23622 well permit.Mountain Energy is cleaning out the 9 wheelie trailers that the 3 Marcellus wells were flowing back into.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity of 0.16-0.74 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS 5.Air temp 36FJLP

Violation ID: 948148
Permit API: 047-24636
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 10/13/2011. There is a second active well (047-24587) on this pad for which drilling operations were completed on 9/16/2011. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0024 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-half of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are four steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. A well development impoundment (Impoundment # 6) is located approximately 3800’ northeast of the HM2 well site (41.53798¿ / -78.70414¿). This impoundment is covered by the same ESCGP that encompasses the HM2 well site. The impoundment has not yet been restored, and greater than nine months have passed since the last well was serviced by this impoundment. The Department does not have record showing that this well development impoundment has been registered, as is required by Chapter 78a.59b(b). The access road leading to this well site and well development impoundment is in general holding up to current traffic levels. There are isolated areas of scouring that should be addressed in an effort to avoid potential E&S issues in the future. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to Bear Creek and several unnamed tributaries. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site & well development impoundment, as well as the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site & well development impoundment.

Inspection Date: 6/08/2021
Comments: Onsite for an incident response to a reported release from the operator. The release was reported at 2:05pm on Monday, 6/7/2021. The release to the ground occurred as a result of the 4 1/2" casing pressuring up during routine maintenance on the well with a service rig. The 2" tubing was blown down prior to the incident. The estimated volume of oil released to the ground is 30 gallons. Consisting of pooled oil and misted oil around the rig and wellhead and spreading out within the hay field approximately 65-80 feet from the well. Approximately 19 gallons of pooled oil was collected and placed into the production tank. The vegetation (hay) that was covered with the mist of oil was cut down and bagged up for disposal. The majority of the impacted area was scrapped up with an excavator and loaded into a triaxle truck for disposal. Clean fill onsite was being applied to the excavated area as part of the cleanup/reclamation. The cleanup operation will continue Violations cite.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8170466
Permit API: 083-56057
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Corydon Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/03/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to reported concerns at the tank battery located near this well.This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack, the well's API number is displayed on the jack. A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl stock tank and a plastic brine tank within an earthen containment is located beside the well. There is evidence of heavy deer activity inside and outside of the containment in the vicinity of the brine tank. Specific conductance (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment is near 1000 uS/cm and the SPC of the soil on the exterior of the containment berm is also elevated (~800 uS/cm). This indicates that the fluid released inside the containment has seeped through the containment wall. Water in the ditch just outside of the containment also has elevated SPC (~ 1300 uS/cm). The elevated SPC readings were detected in an approximate 3' x 10' section of the ditch that also has signs of heavy deer activity. There is no apparent impact to the ditch beyond where the deer tracks are present, as SPC concentrations of the water quickly return to background levels.There is currently a minimal amount of fluid in the brine tank, there are no structural issues apparent with the tank or plumbing. I contacted TJ Allshouse and he agreed to an upcoming field meeting to further investigate the matter.Upon discovering the source, amount and extent of the releases at this tank battery, appropriate remediation options will be explored and documented in upcoming inspections. The inability for the tank battery to contain fluid inside of it will also need to be addressed for compliance to be achieved.

Comments: On December 18, 2025, the Department conducted a follow-up inspection to IR 4106458 at the former location of the MAWC well site in Springfield Township, Fayette County. A violation that was issued in issued in IR 4084771 was left outstanding in IR 4106458, for failure to have a written restoration plan narrative onsite. The remaining violations issued in IR 4084771 were not left outstanding in IR 4106458, as they could not be evaluated due to the snow cover during the time of IR 4106458. The Department requested an NOV Response to IR 4084771 from the operator by December 4, 2025. However, no formal response to IR 4084771 has been received to-date from the operator.The First Modification to the COA was entered on May 1, 2025. Paragraph 3i of the 12/16/2021 CO and A states: "M4 shall immediately commence work to completely restore the Well sites upon execution of the First Amendment and complete restoration of the Well Sites by October 30, 2025, in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas act, 58 Pa.C.S. 3216, the site restoration regulations set forth in 25 Pa. Code 78a.65, and all applicable provisions of the Clean Streams Law and the regulations promulgated thereunder. M4 shall submit form 8000 PM-OOGN0075, "Well Site Restoration Report," within sixty (60) days of restoring the Well Sites."Site restoration is to be conducted "as closely to original conditions as practicable, including restoration of original contours and capability of supporting land uses existing prior to drilling of the Well(s) by October 30, 2025, unless M4 obtains a signed and notarized written consent of the landowner to leave the Well Site in an altered state".The following was observed:The Act 9 sign has been removed from the entrance of the pre-existing access road (photo 1). The access road is to remain unrestored, as it predates construction of the well site (photos 2-4). Temporary stabilization is inconsistent throughout the former well site, as large areas of exposed soil were observed on the slopes at the northern and southern site boundaries (photos 7, 8, 15, and 16). No loose sediment was observed in the rock-lined channels that empty into the pre-existing Sediment Trap (photos 9 and 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed at the northern and southern boundaries (photos 9, 11, 17, and 19). The improperly installed super silt fence which was identified in IR 4084771 remains, with the fabric having completely detached and fallen to the ground (photo 18). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation was observed on site during this inspection. No restoration plans were found on site during this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator reassess whether the E and S controls installed on site are adequate for this well site restoration.The Department also continues to recommend that the operator apply additional temporary stabilization where bare soil is exposed.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4084771 shall remain outstanding. An additional violation shall be issued against the lack of adequate temporary stabilization at the northern and southern site boundaries.

Comments Arrived at the site at 10:20 AM in response to a release of flowback fluid that was discovered at 10:05 on 8/1/12. Jason Petlock of SWN reported the release to the Department on 8-1-12. The initial report indicated the amount of flowback fluid released was determined to be (100-5,000) gallons. A sump has been constructed in this area with a pump located on a liner to recover the fluid. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/21/2023 to PETRO ERIE INC in Sugarcreek Borough, Venango county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PETRO ERIE INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/21/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8153362
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/21/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Comments: On 2/28/20 at 1250 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Diversified Production, LLC's J Budd Overman 5 well (API 063-35887) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. in response to a reported release of approximately 30 gallons of production fluid from a tank located onsite. The release occured on 2/25/20 and was immediately reported to the Department. The release primarily stayed within the secondary containment, with some material making it to an adjacent agricultural field. The operator reported that the tank may have been compromised by a small caliber projectile or shot pellet, which caused the release. The tank was not located onsite at the time of my inspection. The operator stated the tank was pumped out and taken to the shop for repairs. The release of production fluids from a tank onto the ground constitutes violations of SWMA 301, SWMA 302(A), SWMA 610(1), and 78.57(a). The violations will be resolved upon remediation of the impacted area, temporary stabilization of the well site, and submission of disposal receipts to the Department.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/13/2025
Comments: On 03/13/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 03/13/2025 Range Resources Representative, Dennis Furmanek, reported an approximately 84-gallon release of frack fluid off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representative, Matthew Dorsey, was on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Dorsey informed the Department that the release was discovered today (03/13/2025) at approximately 5:00 am, that the quantity released was approximately 84 gallons, and that some of the fluid had since been removed via vacuum truck. The source of release was determined to be a hole in the manifold of a blender, located on the southwestern side of the well pad. The release occurred from the damaged blender, filled and overtopped the primary containment, filled and overtopped the secondary containment, and was release onto the pad aggregate. Mr. Dorsey stated that the cleanup will commence after the frac is completed and equipment is removed in approximately 8 days.Range Resources representative, Dennis Furmanek, contacted via phone call to provide updates. Mr. Furmanek stated that a large sump will be dug behind the spill site on the southwestern end of the well pad to collect any remaining fluids and remediation will begin next week after tear down is complete. He stated that he would notify the Department when the cleanup will begin.Mr. Furmanek also stated that he believed the elevated readings that were obtained from the driving lane on the eastern side of the pad and near the site entrance were caused from road salt that had been tracked onto the site from the large number of sand trucks. He stated that the area in which the elevated readings were observed was the same area in which the sand trucks consistently traveled and parked. He also stated the area had recently been sprayed with water to reduce the dust, which would explain the mud observed in those areas that were exhibiting elevated conductivity.Conductivity probe calibrated on 03/13/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-Large amounts of pooled fluid and mud were observed on a driving lane near the site entrance on the eastern side of the well pad. Elevated field conductivity readings of 3.37 ms/cm and 4.43 ms/cm were observed (Photos 3-8).-The mixer where the release originated, the secondary containments, and the surrounding areas were observed. The extent of impact could not be determined because much of the impacted area was located beneath the secondary containment. A small sump and hose were observed, located in the impacted area beneath the white plastic sheeting covering the temporary waterline. Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 4.29 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 4-16).-Pooled fluid was observed in tire tracks near the site entrance. Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the area. Elevated field screening values of 2.48 ms/cm and 2.93 ms/cm were observed. Non-elevated field conductivity screening values of 78.5 s/cm and 1,189 s/cm were observed on either side of the temporary water line (Photos 17-20).Determination:Violations issued.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a INCIDENT inspection at the Tilden Marcellus -Pierson 801 Well Pad located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 9/30/2019 @1300 hours in response to spill notification# 345263. The weather was 72 degrees, light rain. The spill notification report states, "Regina Logue, Regulatory/Environmental Manager for Tilden Marcellus LLC notified the phone duty officer that a spill of production water from a defective tee in a dump line occurred on 9/28/2019 at 0830 hours. The spill of 1.5 barrels occurred on the well pad. Tilden employees used a vac truck to remove liquid. Lined dumpsters and an excavator are on the way for cleanup. Tilden's well tender will be overseeing the cleanup." As of today's inspection, the area of the spill appears to be backfilled with gravel. Standing fluid on the pad surface in the area of the release had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. A visible flow path, from the spill location, down the fill slope through the vegetation was observed. A "Growline" soil conductivity meter was then used to test the soils in the vicinity of the flow path. The soil readings were >4.0mS/cm which is the max range of the soil meter. The elevated soil conductivity readings reached the area, at the base of the fill slope, beneath a large conifer tree. I immediately left the site to contact my Supervisor, Matt Nuss, to notify him of my findings. I then contaced Jenn Compton, Tilden Marcellus, to inquire as to why the area had been backfilled if the spill had not been remediated and Tilden Marcellus had not followed the procedure to demonstrate attainment of Act 2 standards. Ms. Compton stated she was not onsite for the cleanup over the weekend and when she checked on it this morning, she checked the wrong location onsite near the well head. She stated she had a crew and more waste containers on their way to the site to begin cleanup. I departed the area at 1430 hours. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time against the 2H well API#117-20309: 25 Pa Code 78a.57 SWMA 301 CSL402

Comments Steve Watson, Environmental Health and Safety Specialist of Cabot Oil and Gas contacted me at 12:37 PM on 11/23/15 to report a spill of (68) gallons of production fluid that occurred around 10:30 PM on 11/22/15. Mr. Watson stated that sand washed out of a ball valve on a dump line due to mechanical failure releasing production fluid out of the J Reynen 6H Gas Production Unit onto the concrete containment for the GPU and eventually to the pad surface below the GPU. Apparently the failure of the valve immediately created a flash fire on this GPU. Mr. Watson claimed he was not made aware of the spill on 11/22/15. He investigated the incident during the morning hours on 11/23/15. A truck driver discovered the fire while on-site in the process of unloading production fluid from the production fluid tanks. The driver reported the fire to Cabot upon discovery. The GPU was significantly damaged from the fire. There is staining observed on the concrete containment and a small amount of fluid pooled on the backside of the GPU unit. Failure to collect the brine and other fluids produced during the operation and service of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by DEP.

Comments: Routine site inspection on November 14, 2023 with Evan Buck of DEP. During our inspection we inspected both the well pad and freshwater impoundment (FWI). The operator was issued a new ESCGP3 (ESG291421001-00) in April 2021 which incorporates storm water features and a slight well pad reduction. To date, these new features in the ESCGP3 haven't been completed. The well pad remains at full built-out size with gravel throughout the well pad. The FWI remains intact with >8ft. freeboard. No E and S issues were observed. Both the well pad and FWI appear stable.There are 3 producing Marcellus wells located on this well pad. Well cellars have been backfilled with gravel. There are three gas production units (GPUs) onsite. Gas from each GPU is metered before discharging into Superior Appalachian's 8" steel pipeline. There are (3) 400 BBL produced fluids tanks stationed on the well pad in a modular secondary containment. The Department recommends labeling the produced fluids tanks. Approximately 4" of water was observed in the secondary containment system with a conductivity reading of 390 uS/cm. Rust was observed on the exterior or the produced fluids tanks. The Department recommends monitoring the tanks and repainting or replacing the tanks if needed. A skid mounted compressor unit is located onsite. Stained gravel was observed near the skid mounted compressor unit (pictures 4-7). The stained gravel extends the entire length of the compressor unit and several feet away from the unit. Visible drips on the gravel were observed which appear to be coolant and oil. Two different oil mats were laying near the compressor unit, saturated in oil. One on the front side and one on the back side of the unit. I observed similar oil stains in my April 24, 2023 inspection (3536704). A drum of coolant was observed near the compressor unit not in secondary containment. The Department recommends that all drums be labeled and placed in secondary containment. During the inspection, I reached out to Bob Liddle of LPR and told Mr. Liddle of our findings. Violations have been cited. Due to the unknown amount of oil and coolant released to the ground, the Department encourages the operator to pursue the Act 2 process for site remediation.

Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.

Permit API: 125-22753
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/08/2023
Comments: On 11/08/2023, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Morris F25 well. The following was observed:Operator and well information on site (Photos 1, 2). I recommend placing the rest of the well information on the same sign that has the operator information.Pumpjack in motion upon arrival, some grease/oil on gravel. I recommend removal (Photo 3). Wellhead, production equipment were in generally good condition (Photos 2-5). Mild corrosion. Additional equipment adjacent to the well approximately 40 feet away - there is a depression around the equipment and it is filled with water; dead vegetation around depression, no high conductivity reading. I recommend addressing the depression and exploring the cause of the depression and dead vegetation - unclear if cause if from equipment or pooled water (Photos 6).Downslope of the well were five production tanks within an earthen berm. The berm was in generally good condition, however the pooled water within the berm contained high conductivity readings, specifically in front of tank 1. The sediment within the berm had adequate readings, however the rest of the pooled water had slightly elevated readings. A slightly elevated conductivity reading was taken within the gravel/sediment below the valve of tank 5. This area was relatively small and is recommended that any affected material is removed and disposed of properly. A corroded piece of equipment noted near tank 5 (Photos 7-22, see captions for specific locations). I notified the operator while onsite; a vac truck later was there removing the fluid as I was leaving. Plans are to add equipment to catch fluids when the vac truck removes the hose from the valves. It is noted that the access road has multiple uses, including agricultural, however the access roads to the well sites require routine monitoring and maintenance.Due to the observation of elevated conductivity readings within the pooled water and prompt remediation, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b) are being noted and were immediately corrected. A follow up inspection to ensure there is not residual production fluids within the berm. No additional violations are being issued right now, however additional violations may be forthcoming.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Seneca Resources Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-16
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 862213
Permit API: 117-21688
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Delmar Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-09-16
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted a Follow-up inspection of the Seneca Resources - DCNR 007 Pad K located in Delmar Twp, Tioga Co. on 9/16/2019 @1100 hours. Activity onsite consisted of a truck removing the last temporary tank/gas buster onsite. A Nuverra vac truck was also observed parked onsite. No personnel was observed. At the time of this inspection, the pad surface appears to have been regraded. All temporary flowback equipment appears to have been removed from the site. Multiple damp areas and smalll puddles were observed on the pad surface in the vicinity of the production tanks. The field conductivity of the puddles was recorded at between 5.00mS/cm – 7.5mS/cm.(See attached photos for exact measurements and location of puddles). Courses of silt-sock were observed installed along the NE corner of the pad. Pad material appears to have been eroding off the surface down the fill slope in multiple areas. During a 5/21/19 inspection (IR#2885486) of the site, numerous puddles were discovered on the pad surface. Field screening indicated the conductivity ranged from 4 to >19.99 mS/cm. A sample was collected and upon the DEP receiving the results, they were communicated to Seneca and documented in an Administrative Inspection report (IR# 2897380) on 6/24/19. These results show elevated levels of chloride, strontium and barium indicating a release of a pollutional substance that exceeds Act 2 standards. This inspection report noted violations and requested information pertaining to the quantity of material released to the pad surface as well as what actions Seneca has done to remediate these releases. The NOV response received on 7/15/19 from Seneca failed to provide this information. Therefore, the violations cited will remain outstanding he 73H well permit. Seneca should reference 78a66(c) to determine the actions necessary to achieve compliance at this location. I departed the site @1245 hours.
